transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Ruiz (CTO - MedSync), Priya Menon (ML Engineer), Anita Gupta (IT Ops)
Recording id: ff-20260914-8472

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Onboarding progress: staging infra mostly ready; awaiting VPC peering + CI service account grant.
- Access: KMS key policy needs approval, RBAC roles to be confirmed.

- Next steps: share pricing/SOW, Maya to send infra runbook, customer to grant access and upload eval set.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for making time today, uh we'll do a quick sync on the pilot, onboarding, and env readiness, I think we have about 45 minutes, is that still good?
[00:06] Carlos: yep that's perfect, we've blocked the time, thanks.
[00:10] Maya: hi all, Maya here, I'll jump into the infra checklist in a bit.
[00:13] Priya: hi, Priya, looking forward to walking through the tuning notes.
[00:16] Anita: Anita from ITops, I'll track the access items.

[02:05] Jordan: quick recap of where we left off last week, customer uploaded sample dataset, Redwood spun up dedicated staging nodes in our dedicated pool for the pilot, we also provided temporary API keys for early runs. Carlos, did you get a chance to spin up the staging bucket with the 1k records?
[02:22] Carlos: yes we did, Priya put them in s3-staging-med-sync, might be a bit messy, uh filenames are inconsistent but it's there.
[02:30] Priya: yeah sorry about naming, we had two exporters, will normalize by end of day.

[04:10] Maya: infra checklist quick: we need VPC peering for low-latency egress, CI service account added to the staging project's IAM so our agents can pull model artifacts, and KMS key policy updated to allow Redwood's ded-ops role to unwrap. small note: the KMS policy must be a customer-managed key with grant for 1 month for pilot.
[04:35] Anita: on the KMS we actually prefer HSM-backed keys, but for pilot we can do a customer-managed key in AWS KMS, I'll need the exact principal string from you.
[04:45] Maya: sure, I'll paste the principal in the slack thread after this call. it's redwood-ci@redwood-infra.svc. I might have missed the exact namespace but I'll confirm.

[06:00] Jordan: one ask on the security side, we also sent the SOC2 + ISO doc set last week, did your security team have any follow-up?
[06:08] Carlos: they skimmed it, they had some qs about audit log retention and whether we get token-level telemetry, can you confirm we get token-level cost breakdown in the console?
[06:20] Jordan: yes, the console surfaces per-request token and latency breakdowns, and we can export logs to your SIEM, there's a toggle in the console for log export. I'll include a screenshot in the follow up.

[08:15] Priya: on the model side, we did a couple of runs against the non-quantized variant and saw median latency around 420ms per large prompt payload, however tail P95 spiked to 1.2s under concurrent sim. Those numbers from Redwood's hosted test cluster or the dedicated pilot nodes?
[08:32] Maya: that's from your dedicated pilot nodes we've provisioned, small caveat transcription, um, the patch we applied had different kernel selection, so the P95 is a bit inflated because caching wasn't fully primed. once KV cache warms up we expect P95 to be lower.
[08:48] Priya: okay that aligns with what we saw locally. Did you enable continuous batching?
[08:52] Maya: yes we have continuous batching on by default for the pilot profile, but the batch sizing is conservative — we can tune it. also we tried the 4-bit quantized model that reduces memory but introduced slight quality diffs on recitals.

[10:10] Carlos: quality diffs are a concern for clinicians - we can't have hallucinations on discharge summaries. What kind of evals do you recommend?
[10:18] Maya: recommend sets: intent preservation, hallucination sensitivity, and entity fidelity — Priya, we asked you for a prompt set last week?
[10:25] Priya: yes uploaded 150 prompts, will add another 850 by EOD.

[12:00] Jordan: commercial / pricing note: pilot pricing is usage-based plus a small reserved capacity commit for the dedicated nodes. I'm going to share an updated pricing sheet after the call; if you want an enterprise SOW we can draft one.
[12:15] Carlos: budget looks okay but we need the SOW for procurement. procurement will want a 60-day pilot window and a clear exit clause.
[12:25] Jordan: fine we can do a 60-day pilot with an explicit data deletion and key revocation workflow.

[14:30] Anita: regarding network we prefer VPC peering over public endpoints, how do you authenticate the peered connection for model downloads?
[14:40] Maya: model artifacts are pulled over the peered VPC using signed tokens and the CI service account; we can restrict egress via SG rules. also we support on-prem node packaging if needed but that adds ops overhead.
[14:55] Anita: ok we'll trial peering first.

[17:05] Priya: quick on tuning, we tried quantization to int4 and saw a 30% cost reduction but slight degradation on entity extraction tests, need to run a calibrator and maybe mixed precision for specific layers.
[17:22] Maya: right, we normally recommend a mixed approach: int8 quant for encoder layers and fp16 for decoder to preserve entity fidelity. we also can enable per-route model variants so sensitive tasks route to non-quantized model.
[17:40] Carlos: that routing sounds useful. will that increase complexity in routing rules?
[17:44] Maya: it's baked into the console, you can define policy by tag, latency, or cost thresholds, and there's automatic fallback to hosted variants. small note: UI may show 'Redwood Dedicate' spelled weirdly in some older screens, ignore that.

[20:00] Jordan: can we talk about benchmarks? We propose a benchmark run with your 10k/day profile next week. We'll do three runs: cold start, warmed KV cache, and sustained throughput 100 QPS.
[20:12] Priya: sounds good. For cold start can you confirm we should seed the cache with the top 200 prefixes?
[20:18] Maya: yes seeding helps; we'll provide a seeding script. we'll also capture token-level cost, latency distribution, and tail latencies.

[22:30] Anita: on RBAC, who should be in the Redwood admin group for the pilot? We prefer two admins from our side: Carlos and Anita only.
[22:40] Jordan: that's fine. we'll create a minimal RBAC role for your admins and a read-only for others.

[24:55] Carlos: any outstanding security docs we need?
[24:58] Jordan: we have SOC2, ISO, pen test summary, and network diagram. I'll attach them in the follow-up slack thread and also push to your SSO space.

[26:10] Priya: question about telemetry retention, how long do you keep detailed traces by default?
[26:18] Maya: detailed request traces are 30 days by default; logs can be exported to your SIEM for longer retention. we also support per-customer retention settings as an add-on.

[28:05] Jordan: ok let's run through the short checklist and owners. VPC peering (Customer, owner Anita), KMS policy update (Customer + Redwood, Anita + Maya), service account grant (Customer, Carlos), upload eval set (Customer, Priya), pricing/SOW (Redwood, Jordan), benchmark scheduling (joint, Maya+Priya).
[28:30] Anita: noted. we'll start the KMS approval in our ticketing system and should have it by Thursday.

[30:50] Priya: on eval metrics, can Redwood provide a small script that computes entity recall/precision from outputs?
[30:58] Maya: yes we have an eval harness we can share — it's in the shared drive link: https://redwood.example.com/pilot-eval-harness (placeholder). it computes BLEU-like and entity-F1 metrics and can ingest your CSV.

[33:00] Jordan: minor admin: we'll need a signed MSA to start the pilot officially; I'll attach a redlined SOW with the pricing sheet. procurement wants to see data deletion language and one month KMS key revocation process.
[33:14] Carlos: procurement is okay as long as we can revoke keys and they can't retain copies, so process is important.

[35:20] Maya: performance notes: based on current model and vm shapes, we foresee 15-20% cost reduction after tuning batch sizes and enabling prefix caching. but if you prioritize latency, we can reduce batching — tradeoff is higher per-token cost.
[35:40] Priya: we care about latency for patient-facing summaries, cost is secondary; let's target median <500ms and P95 <900ms.
[35:50] Maya: noted, we'll tune toward latency SLOs.

[38:10] Jordan: wrap-up, we'll do the benchmark next week, Jordan will send SOW, Maya will send infra runbook and principal strings, Priya will finish eval prompts and upload. Anita and Carlos to confirm access grant.
[38:30] Carlos: quick nit, competitors: we did a compare vs Anthropic last month and liked Anthropic on safety metrics, but Redwood's perf numbers and observability are a big reason to pilot.
[38:45] Jordan: totally — we can run an apples-to-apples benchmark against any model family you choose.

[40:05] Priya: small request, can you enable token-level cost export to our billing bucket so procurement can see daily cost breakdown?
[40:12] Jordan: yes we'll enable export, I'll include the steps in the follow-up.

[42:00] Anita: ok that's all from my side.
[42:03] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the runbook and pricing.
[42:10] Jordan: thanks team. recap of next steps will be in email and I'll create the calendar invite for the benchmark run.

[44:30] (call ends)
